model.title: 'More of a challenge than a lecture.' How far do you agree?

parts.text: Evidence: 'I am not asking anyone to throw their phone into the sea.'
Explain: the writer avoids preaching by rejecting an extreme demand
Balance: however, the rhetorical questions do press the reader
Conclusion: overall, the closing challenge 'Try it for a week' feels like an invitation

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: I largely agree: by refusing an extreme demand, the writer avoids lecturing, though the rhetorical questions do press us; overall, 'Try it for a week' feels like an invitation.

questions.q: Find your weakest question and name its skill
Core: DIRT: rewrite your weakest answer using the model, in a different colour
Extend: correct two shorter answers and explain the corrections
Stretch: write a one-sentence rule for evaluation questions
questions.a: For example: judge, prove, weigh, conclude

questions.q: What most improves an evaluation answer?
questions.a: A) weighing evidence before a judgement. Evaluation needs evidence weighed to reach a judgement.
